Today, on Veterans Day, we honor the courage, dedication, and sacrifice of every Virgin Islander who has served our country.

Generations of Virgin Islanders have worn the uniform, serving in every branch and in conflicts around the world, and they continue to serve our community long after they come home. We are proud of them, and we are grateful to their families, who sacrificed alongside them.

Honoring our veterans means more than words. Too many Virgin Islands veterans still have to travel off-island for specialty care, and access to services and benefits in the territory remains a challenge. That’s why I’m committed to strengthening VA care here at home, cutting through red tape, and ensuring every veteran and family receives the care, benefits, and opportunities they have earned.

To every Virgin Islands veteran: thank you for your service. 💙

May the Festival of Lights bring joy, peace, prosperity, and new beginnings to you and your loved ones. 

Wishing everyone celebrating a bright and beautiful holiday! https://t.co/TcR9KYmbUl

Behind every servicemember is a family, and in the Virgin Islands, military service runs deep in our families and our history.

This November, during Military Family Month, we honor the spouses, children, parents, and grandparents who make sacrifices so their loved ones can serve. They manage households through deployments, distance, and the added challenges of island life, from limited access to services to the long distances between them and military installations on the mainland.

We also recognize the families of our Virgin Islands National Guard, who stand by their loved ones as they deploy overseas and serve our own community through hurricanes and recovery.

Thank you to every Virgin Islands military family. We see you, and we are grateful. 💙

Liberty Day reminds us that our voices matter. 

David Hamilton Jackson used the power of the press to demand justice for Virgin Islanders, and that work continues today. 

Let's keep honoring his legacy by speaking up for our community. #BullAndBread #LibertyDay https://t.co/rxDdoTLZFS

48 million Americans, including 1 in 5 children, experience food insecurity, and families right here in the Virgin Islands feel that strain every day at the grocery store. No one should go to bed hungry. 🌱

Supporting our local farmers and growing more of our own food is how we build a stronger, more food-secure Virgin Islands. And in Congress, House Democrats are working to restore food assistance to the millions of Americans, including Virgin Islanders, who lost it.

Today and every day, we recognize and celebrate the cultures, histories, and contributions of Indigenous peoples.

Long before these islands were called the Virgin Islands, they were home to the Ciboney, Taíno, and Carib (Kalinago) peoples, who fished our waters, farmed our land, and built thriving communities across St. Croix, St. Thomas, and St. John. Their legacy lives on in our landscape: in the petroglyphs carved at Reef Bay on St. John, in the ceremonial grounds uncovered at Cinnamon Bay, and at Salt River Bay on St. Croix, where Carib warriors stood their ground in 1493 in one of the first recorded acts of Indigenous resistance to European arrival in the Americas.

On Indigenous Peoples' Day, we honor these first Virgin Islanders, whose history is part of our history, and the Indigenous communities whose traditions have endured across generations and continue to shape our territory and our country.

This LGBTQ+ History Month, we celebrate the generations of LGBTQ+ people who have fought for equality and helped move our country forward. 

We honor their history and continue the work toward a future where everyone can live openly and freely. https://t.co/fqdV7Q8B1u

posts.text:
Today, October 1, Virgin Islanders honor Contract Day.

After our ancestors took their freedom from chattel slavery in 1848, the Labor Act of 1849 created a new kind of bondage. Workers were bound to one plantation for a full year, with a day wage and restricted movement, able to change estates only on Contract Day. It was freedom in name only.

On October 1, 1878, when rumors of reform proved false, 30 years of frustration ignited the St. Croix Labor Rebellion, known to us as Fireburn. It was led by four women we revere as our Queens: Mary Thomas, Mathilda McBean, Susanna "Bottom Belly" Abrahamson, and Axeline "Queen Agnes" Salomon.

They demanded fair wages and the repeal of the Labor Act, and many paid with their lives. From their sacrifice came reforms that dismantled the labor system.

Today we honor our heritage and remember their courage. 🔥

G’mar Chatima Tovah to all observing Yom Kippur. 

May this sacred day of reflection and renewal bring peace and meaning to you and your loved ones. https://t.co/yBP4t0EN1G

Today, we celebrate Constitution Day and the founding document that established the framework of our democracy and enshrined our fundamental rights and freedoms. 

We must continue working to uphold our Constitution and protect the rights it guarantees to every American. https://t.co/n8iq7o9x5E

Your voice matters, and your vote is your voice. 

This National Voter Registration Day, make sure you’re registered, encourage your friends and family to register, and make a plan to participate in our democracy. https://t.co/8NcAu7s7vk

Shanah Tovah U'Metuka to everyone in the Virgin Islands and abroad celebrating Rosh Hashanah! 

May the New Year bring you and your loved ones peace, health, reflection, and renewal. https://t.co/qtswRpbo7H

On the anniversary of September 11, we pause to remember those we lost and honor the heroes who put their lives on the line to save others. 

I am committed to supporting the first responders, survivors, and families who continue to carry the legacy of that tragedy https://t.co/niETe2JnF0

Hispanic Heritage Month is an opportunity to celebrate the traditions and achievements of Hispanic Americans and recognize the many ways they have shaped our nation and, more specifically our Virgin Islands home. 

This month and always, we celebrate the diversity and contributions that make our communities stronger.

September is Suicide Prevention Month. By checking in on one another, talking openly about mental health, and making sure people can access the care they need, we can help prevent suicide and remind those who are struggling that they are not alone.

If you or someone you know needs help, reach out to 988.

Happy Labor Day! Today, we honor the workers whose skill, dedication, and contributions keep our communities and economy moving. 

We will continue advocating for the creation good-paying jobs, and fight for strong worker protections and an economy where hard work pays off. https://t.co/lmoNQaokcJ

On July 30, 1965, Medicare and Medicaid were signed into law, expanding access to health care for millions of Americans. 

Over 6 decades later, House Democrats are still fighting to protect and strengthen these vital programs and ensure access to quality and affordable health care.

On Mandela Day, we honor the life and legacy of Nelson Mandela. 

His fight for justice lives on and his memory continues to instill in us a steadfast commitment to racial equality, human rights, and democracy. https://t.co/djAYm9WwlV

Six years ago, we lost the Conscience of the Congress, Congressman John Lewis.

From leading the march across the Edmund Pettus Bridge to serving in the House, he never stopped fighting for justice, equality, and the right to vote. 

We honor his legacy by carrying it forward. https://t.co/sTGpDGCZwQ

On the anniversary of Obergefell v. Hodges, we honor the advocates and couples whose courage helped secure marriage equality across the United States and recommit ourselves to protecting LGBTQI+ rights. 

We will defend the rights and dignity of LGBTQI+ Americans and push back against the right-wing extremism that discriminates against Americans.

Today we celebrate the fathers and father figures who show up every day with care, wisdom, and dedication. 

Wishing everyone a Happy Father’s Day! https://t.co/1K1q1Q3xLe

Being Caribbean American means carrying two worlds in your heart — and showing up for both. 

This Caribbean American Heritage Month, I'm reflecting on what it truly means to be from these islands and to serve in the halls of Congress. The richness of our culture, our people, our resilience — it shapes everything I do.

Stay with me through the rest of this month as I share what being Caribbean American means to me. ✨

#CaribbeanAmericanHeritageMonth #CAHM #USVirginIslands #Caribbean #StaceyPlaskett #ProudlyCaribbean

On June 19, 1865, news of the Emancipation Proclamation reached the last enslaved people in Galveston, Texas. 

Juneteenth is both a celebration of freedom and a reminder of our ongoing work and responsibility to advance equality and justice for all. https://t.co/MaKQ7f97rN
Today we celebrate Flag Day and honor the Stars and Stripes as a symbol of our nation’s enduring values and aspirations. https://t.co/pA2YPkb0RY

Today, we honor the women who have served, sacrificed, and strengthened our nation in uniform. 
June 12 is Women Veterans Recognition Day — celebrating 250 years of service, strength, and sisterhood. 🇺🇸 

Photo courtesy of the Military Women's Memorial. https://t.co/mA2ywk5dVP

Cicely Tyson didn't just perform — she made a statement every time she stepped on screen.

The daughter of immigrants from the Caribbean island of Nevis, she spent seven decades refusing to let Hollywood define what a Black woman's story could look like. Every role was intentional. Every choice was deliberate. And every performance reminded the world of something it needed to see.

A Caribbean daughter. An American icon. A standard that still stands. 💙

#CaribbeanAmericanHeritageMonth

When the country needed someone to lead the charge on health equity during one of the most critical moments in modern history, a daughter of St. Thomas answered the call.

Dr. Marcella Nunez-Smith has spent her career fighting for the communities medicine too often overlooks — including the Caribbean territories she calls home. Brilliant, dedicated, and rooted in purpose, she is proof that where you come from can fuel exactly the work the world needs from you.

The Virgin Islands raised her. The nation needed her. 💙

#CaribbeanAmericanHeritageMonth

Before there was a blueprint, there was Shirley Chisholm.

The daughter of Caribbean immigrants, she walked into the U.S. Congress in 1968 as the first Black woman ever elected to serve as a Member of Congress— and then dared to run for President four years later. 

She didn't ask for permission. She didn't wait for the door to open. She kicked it down and left it open for everyone who came after.

Unbought. Unbossed. Unforgettable. 💙
#CaribbeanAmericanHeritageMonth
